name: Celecoxib
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Celecoxib is a cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) selective nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) cleared mainly by liver metabolism (CYP2C9). Like other NSAIDs it can cause acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, fluid retention and hypertension. The US label gives no dose change for mild to moderate kidney impairment and does not recommend it in severe renal insufficiency, which was not studied.
kidney_function_basis: Label states kidney function qualitatively (mild, moderate, severe renal insufficiency); the PK study used GFR 35–60 mL/min. Mapping 'severe' to CrCl <30 is our judgment.

bands.recommendation: Usual dose by indication (osteoarthritis 200 mg/day; rheumatoid arthritis 100 to 200 mg twice daily). Lowest effective dose, shortest duration (label).

No dose change in the label for mild to moderate impairment (AUC about 40% lower at GFR 35–60). NSAIDs reduce kidney blood flow: monitor creatinine, potassium and blood pressure; avoid with volume depletion and avoid combining with ACE inhibitors or ARBs plus diuretics.
bands.short: No dose change; monitor SCr, K, BP

bands.recommendation: Not recommended in severe renal insufficiency (label 8.7); not studied. Avoid in advanced kidney disease unless benefits outweigh the risk of worsening kidney function (label 5.6).
Not recommended in severe renal insufficiency (label 8.7); not studied. Avoid in advanced kidney disease unless benefits outweigh the risk of worsening kidney function (label 5.6).

hd.text: Not recommended (severe renal insufficiency; label). Not studied in dialysis. NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

pd.text: Not recommended (severe renal insufficiency; label). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Avoid: NSAIDs can worsen acute kidney injury; severe renal insufficiency not recommended (label).

dialyzable: Unlikely: no data, but over 97% protein-bound, so hemodialysis is unlikely to help in overdose (label 10).
monitoring: Creatinine, potassium and blood pressure in CKD, heart failure, liver disease, dehydration or with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics (label 5.6). Edema and heart failure. Hemoglobin if anemia symptoms.

pediatric.approved_ages: Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (JRA), 2 years and older, weight 10 kg or more (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: JRA: 10 to 25 kg, 50 mg twice daily; over 25 kg, 100 mg twice daily (label).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney data; label kidney warnings apply to all patients: monitor creatinine, potassium and blood pressure.
renal.short: No dose data; monitor SCr, K

renal.recommendation: Not recommended in severe renal insufficiency (label statement not limited by age).
Not recommended in severe renal insufficiency.

adult: Label does not define 'severe renal insufficiency'; mapped to CrCl <30 by judgment (PK data only at GFR 35–60).
PH strengths 100, 200 and 400 mg capsules match US strengths (US also has 50 mg).
pediatric: Pediatric kidney bands extend the adult label statement (not age-limited) to children; no pediatric kidney study.
